messages:
juan-customer: Hey team — starting ~09:10 UTC we saw vectors/sec drop by ~60% for customer-42 while tokens/sec stayed ~flat. No 5xxs, just slow tails. Request id: req_0a9f. Can you take a look?

emma-support: Thanks Juan — can you paste a minimal request (headers + body) and the region? Also any recent config changes? :thinking_face:

juan-customer: region=us-west-2. Request looks like: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-v1","input":["doc1","doc2"],"batch_size":64}'``` We rolled a client-side batch size tweak yesterday (64 -> 256) but switched back to 64 when we saw the drop.

ryan-eng-ml: Noted. Juan, did you change embedding dim or model variant? The payload above is fine. If tokens/sec is flat but vectors/sec dips, suspect vectorization pipeline batching or GPU slot contention.

juan-customer: No model change. We do occasionally send mixed-length docs. I can repro by replaying traffic to their staging key, should I capture traces?

emma-support: Please capture one slow request trace (include trace id) and any traces where vectors/sec is fine. That will help. @sana can you check infra-side queue depth for the customer's shard around 09:05-09:20?

sana-eng-sre: Looking now. infra-bot: "kafka_consumer_lag: customer-42-shard -> 0/0" — ignore. GPU pool usw2-emb-a shows queue depth spike at 09:08: ~500 pending items for ~45s. Also saw several long-running KV cache locks on host g-12 (`kvcache.lock.hold_avg=1.2s` up from ~30ms).

zara-eng: KV cache lock increases often correlate with many small batches contending for the same prefix. Did the client-side batch size oscillate? A lot of small requests + big ones can cause prefix cache thrashing which increases per-request serialization.

ryan-eng-ml: Also check autoscaler behavior — if GPUs are in burst mode and slots are saturated, we see throughput regressions for vectors even if token generator is okay (because token gen happens on CPU or smaller model path). Can you fetch the slot utilization logs?

sana-eng-sre: Pulled slot utilization: at 09:06-09:12 GPU util jumped to 98% and batch queue length > 40, scheduler moved some flows to fallback variant (rwd-embed-v1-quantized) at 09:09. Fallback lowered vectorization throughput for this workload (different kernel perf).

juan-customer: Hmm we saw no explicit fallback errors in client logs. Any way to pin whether we hit a fallback model?

emma-support: We can correlate model variant in traces. Juan, please share trace id req_0a9f — we'll match server-side model routing. Meanwhile @ryan can you check whether the routing policy could have dropped this customer to quantized variant under high queue depth?

ryan-eng-ml: Confirmed in routing logs: req_0a9f routed to rwd-embed-v1-quantized at 09:08:59 due to policy: low-cost-fallback when gpu_slot_wait_ms > 200. That explains lower vectors/sec. What caused slot wait spike: looks tied to many small batch arrivals plus a KV cache lock on prefix "p:customer-42:docid" that serialized 70 requests.

zara-eng: Root cause likely a confluence: client churn in batch sizes + a hot prefix in KV cache -> KV lock + long scheduler wait -> fallback to quantized model variant. Mitigations: 1) increase client batch size or use batching token; 2) add jitter to avoid thundering herd; 3) on our side, raise lock concurrency for hot prefixes and tweak routing threshold.

emma-support: Juan — recommended short-term: enable client-side batching to 128 and add 10-50ms jitter; we'll patch routing threshold for this shard (increase gpu_slot_wait_ms threshold to 500ms) and bump KV cache concurrency on the affected host.

juan-customer: Will try batching + jitter and report. Any repro steps you want me to run to validate?

sana-eng-sre: Yes — please replay a 10k request sample to staging with your normal arrival pattern but two variants: (A) original bursty (many small batches), (B) aggregated to batch_size=128 + jitter 10-50ms. Measure vectors/sec and freq of quantized fallback. Provide traces for one slow and one fast flow.

juan-customer: Got it — I'll run both tonight and attach traces. Thanks. :pray:

ryan-eng-ml: Internal follow-ups: I'll open a perf card to examine whether quantized variant kernel can be improved for short sequences; also evaluate adaptive routing so fallback only triggers when queue depth sustained > X s.

zara-eng: I'll schedule a hotfix to KV cache concurrency and coordinate with infra.

emma-support: Keeping thread open until Juan confirms repro. Tagging: @oncall (for infra change window).

oncall: Ack — will standby for the KV concurrency bump window.

juan-customer: Update: after batching->128 + jitter, vectors/sec in staging returned to expected baseline and no quantized fallbacks observed in traces. Thanks team! :tada:
